# pastey - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pastey/0.2.3/target-redirect/pastey/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#macros-for-all-your-token-pasting-needs)Macros for all your token pasting needs

`pastey` is the fork of `paste` and is aimed to be a drop-in replacement with additional features for
`paste` crate

## Migrating from `paste` crate

Migrating from `paste` crate to `pastey` is super simple, just change the following
in your `Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
- paste = "1"
+ pastey = "*" # Or any specific version of pastey
```
Or even better way:

```
[dependencies]
- paste = "1"
+ paste = { package = "pastey", version = "*" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

Add `pastey` as your dependency in `Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
# TODO: Replace with latest version available on crates.io
pastey = "*"
```
This approach works with any Rust compiler 1.54+.

[§](https://docs.rs#pasting-identifiers)Pasting identifiers

Within the `paste!` macro, identifiers inside `[<`…`>]` are pasted together to
form a single identifier.

```
use pastey::paste;
paste! {
    // Defines a const called `QRST`.
    const [<Q R S T>]: &str = "success!";
}
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(
        paste! { [<Q R S T>].len() },
        8,
    );
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#more-elaborate-example)More elaborate example

The next example shows a macro that generates accessor methods for some struct fields. It demonstrates how you might find it useful to bundle a paste invocation inside of a macro_rules macro.

```
use pastey::paste;
macro_rules! make_a_struct_and_getters {
    ($name:ident { $($field:ident),* }) => {
        // Define a struct. This expands to:
        //
        //     pub struct S {
        //         a: String,
        //         b: String,
        //         c: String,
        //     }
        pub struct $name {
            $(
                $field: String,
            )*
        }
        // Build an impl block with getters. This expands to:
        //
        //     impl S {
        //         pub fn get_a(&self) -> &str { &self.a }
        //         pub fn get_b(&self) -> &str { &self.b }
        //         pub fn get_c(&self) -> &str { &self.c }
        //     }
        paste! {
            impl $name {
                $(
                    pub fn [<get_ $field>](&self) -> &str {
                        &self.$field
                    }
                )*
            }
        }
    }
}
make_a_struct_and_getters!(S { a, b, c });
fn call_some_getters(s: &S) -> bool {
    s.get_a() == s.get_b() && s.get_c().is_empty()
}
let s = S {
    a: String::from("x"),
    b: String::from("x"),
    c: String::new(),
 };
 assert!(call_some_getters(&s));
 let s2 = S {
     a: String::from("x"),
     b: String::from("y"),
     c: String::new(),
 };
 assert!(!call_some_getters(&s2));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#case-conversion)Case conversion

The `pastey` crate supports the following case modfiers:

| Modifier | Description |
|---|---|
| `$var:lower` | Lower Case |
| `$var:upper` | Upper Case |
| `$var:snake` | Snake Case |
| `$var:camel`or`$var:upper_camel` | Upper Camel Case |
| `$var:lower_camel` | Lower Camel Case [#4](https://github.com/AS1100K/pastey/issues/4) |
| `$var:camel_edge` | Covers Edge cases of Camel Case. [#3](https://github.com/AS1100K/pastey/issues/3) |

**NOTE: The pastey crate is going to be a drop in replacement to paste crate,
and will not change the behaviour of existing modifier like  lower, upper,
snake and camel. For modifying the behaviour new modifiers will be created,
like camel_edge**

You can also use multiple of these modifers like `$var:snake:upper` would give you
`SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.

Example

```
use pastey::paste;
paste! {
    const [<LIB env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"):snake:upper>]: &str = "libpastey";
    let _ = LIBPASTEY;
}
```
The precise Unicode conversions are as defined by [ str::to_lowercase](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_lowercase) and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.to_uppercase)

`str::to_uppercase`[§](https://docs.rs#replace-modifier)Replace modifier

The `replace` modifier allows you to perform string replacement on identifiers,
using the same semantics as [ str::replace](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.replace). This is useful for transforming
identifiers by removing or substituting substrings.

```
use pastey::paste;
macro_rules! m {
    ($(($command:ident, $from:ident)),+) => {
        paste! {
            $(pub struct $command {})*
            pub enum Command {
                $(
                    [< $command:replace($from, "") >] ( $command )
                ),*
            }
        }
    }
}
m! {
    (CommandFoo, Command),
    (CommandBar, Command),
    (HelloWorld, Hello)
}
let command_bar = Command::Bar(CommandBar {});
let command_foo = Command::Foo(CommandFoo {});
let command_hello = Command::World(HelloWorld {});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#raw-identifier-generation)Raw Identifier Generation

`pastey` now supports raw identifiers using a special raw mode. By prefixing a
token with `#` inside the paste syntax, it treats that token as a raw identifier.

```
use pastey::paste;
macro_rules! define_struct_and_impl {
    ($name:ident $(- $name_tail:ident)*) => {
        paste!{
            struct [< # $name:camel $( $name_tail)* >]; // '#' signals a raw identifier
            impl [< # $name:camel $( $name_tail)* >] {
                fn [< # $name:snake $( _ $name_tail:snake)* >]() {}
            }
        }
    }
}
define_struct_and_impl!(loop);
define_struct_and_impl!(loop - xyz);
fn test_fn() {
    let _ = Loop::r#loop();
    let _ = Loopxyz::loop_xyz();
}
test_fn();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pasting-documentation-strings)Pasting documentation strings

Within the `paste!` macro, arguments to a #[doc …] attribute are implicitly
concatenated together to form a coherent documentation string.

```
use pastey::paste;
macro_rules! method_new {
    ($ret:ident) => {
        paste! {
            #[doc = "Create a new `" $ret "` object."]
            pub fn new() -> $ret { $ret {} }
        }
    };
}
pub struct Pastey {}
method_new!(Pastey);  // expands to #[doc = "Create a new `Paste` object"]
let _ = new();
```

This crate is the fork of

[and I appreciate the efforts of](https://github.com/dtolnay/paste)`paste`[@dtolnay](https://github.com/dtolnay)and other contributors.[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

[Apache License, Version 2.0](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE)or[MIT license](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT)at your option.Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this crate by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# riscv_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv-types/0.1.0/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv_types/

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Core](https://docs.rs/trait.CoreInterruptNumber.html)- Interrupt - Number
- Marker trait for enums of target-specific core interrupt numbers.
- [Exception](https://docs.rs/trait.ExceptionNumber.html)- Number
- Trait for enums of target-specific exception numbers.

# CoreInterruptNumber in riscv_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/riscv-types/^0.1.0/trait.CoreInterruptNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait CoreInterruptNumber: `[InterruptNumber](https://docs.rs/trait.InterruptNumber.html) { }## Expand description

Marker trait for enums of target-specific core interrupt numbers.

Core interrupts are interrupts are retrieved from the `mcause` CSR. Usually, vectored mode is
only available for core interrupts. The `riscv` crate provides a default implementation for
the RISC-V ISA. However, a PAC may override the default implementation if the target has a
different interrupt numbering scheme (e.g., ESP32C3).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

Each enum variant must represent a valid core interrupt number read from the `mcause` CSR.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# HartIdNumber in riscv_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/riscv-types/^0.1.0/trait.HartIdNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait HartIdNumber: `[Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) {
    const [MAX_HART_ID_NUMBER](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.MAX_HART_ID_NUMBER): [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
    // Required methods
    fn [number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.number)(self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
[from_number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.from_number)(value: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/result/type.Result.html)<Self>;
}## Expand description

Trait for enums of HART identifiers.

This trait should be implemented by a peripheral access crate (PAC) on its enum of available
HARTs for a specific device. Each variant must convert to a `usize` of its HART ID number.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- This trait must only be implemented on a PAC of a RISC-V target.
- This trait must only be implemented on enums of HART IDs.
- Each enum variant must represent a distinct value (no duplicates are permitted),
- Each anum variant must always return the same value (do not change at runtime).
- All the HART ID numbers must be less than or equal to `MAX_HART_ID_NUMBER`.
- `MAX_HART_ID_NUMBER`must coincide with the highest allowed HART ID number.

## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/riscv/0.16.1/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/

## Expand description

Low level access to RISC-V processors

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv)Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.60 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

This crate provides:

- Access to core registers like `mstatus`or`mcause`.
- Interrupt manipulation mechanisms.
- Wrappers around assembly instructions like `WFI`.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

[§](https://docs.rs#s-mode)`s-mode`

This feature re-exports in `interrupt` S-mode interrupt functions defined in `interrupt::supervisor`.
By default, the crate assumes that the target is running in M-mode.
Thus, `interrupt` re-exports the M-mode functions defined in `interrupt::machine`.

[§](https://docs.rs#critical-section-single-hart)`critical-section-single-hart`

This feature enables a [ critical-section](https://github.com/rust-embedded/critical-section)
implementation suitable for single-hart targets, based on disabling interrupts globally.
This feature uses S-mode interrupt handling if the

`s-mode` feature is enabled, and M-mode otherwise.It is **unsound** to enable it on multi-hart targets,
and may cause functional problems in systems where some interrupts must NOT be disabled
or critical sections are managed as part of an RTOS. In these cases, you should use
a target-specific implementation instead, typically provided by a HAL or RTOS crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#rt)`rt`

This feature enables code related to [ riscv-rt](https://github.com/rust-embedded/riscv/tree/master/riscv-rt)
runtime support in the

`riscv::pac_enum` macro. Namely, it enables the generation of
trap handler functions and dispatch functions.[§](https://docs.rs#rt-v-trap)`rt-v-trap`

This feature enables code related to vectored trap handling in addition to the `rt` feature.
Namely, it enables the generation of a vector table and the corresponding assembly code for core interrupts.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [asm](https://docs.rs/asm/index.html)
- Assembly instructions
- [bits](https://docs.rs/bits/index.html)
- [delay](https://docs.rs/delay/index.html)
- Delay devices and providers
- [interrupt](https://docs.rs/interrupt/index.html)
- Interrupts
- [register](https://docs.rs/register/index.html)
- RISC-V CSR’s
- [result](https://docs.rs/result/index.html)

# riscv::asm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/asm/index.html

## Expand description

Assembly instructions

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [delay](https://docs.rs/fn.delay.html)
- Blocks the program for *at least*`cycles`CPU cycles.
- [ebreak](https://docs.rs/fn.ebreak.html)- ⚠
- `EBREAK`instruction wrapper
- [ecall](https://docs.rs/fn.ecall.html)- ⚠
- `ECALL`instruction wrapper
- [fence](https://docs.rs/fn.fence.html)
- `FENCE`instruction wrapper
- [fence_i](https://docs.rs/fn.fence_i.html)
- `FENCE.I`instruction wrapper
- [nop](https://docs.rs/fn.nop.html)
- `NOP`instruction wrapper
- [sfence_](https://docs.rs/fn.sfence_vma.html)- vma
- `SFENCE.VMA`instruction wrapper
- [sfence_](https://docs.rs/fn.sfence_vma_all.html)- vma_ - all
- `SFENCE.VMA`instruction wrapper (all address spaces and page table levels)
- [wfi](https://docs.rs/fn.wfi.html)
- `WFI`instruction wrapper

# clear in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.clear.html

# Macro clear

[Source](../src/riscv/register/macros.rs.html#376-404) ```
macro_rules! clear {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Convenience macro around the `csrrc` assembly instruction to clear the CSR register.

This macro is intended for use with the [clear_csr](macro.clear_csr.html) or [set_clear_csr](macro.set_clear_csr.html) macros.

---

}

# csr_field_enum in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.csr_field_enum.html

```
macro_rules! csr_field_enum {
    ($(#[$field_ty_doc:meta])*
     $field_ty:ident {
         default: $default_variant:ident,
         $(
             $(#[$field_doc:meta])*
             $variant:ident = $value:expr$(,)?
          )+
     }$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```

# read_composite_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_composite_csr.html

```
macro_rules! read_composite_csr {
    ($hi:expr, $lo:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Convenience macro to read a composite value from a CSR register.

- `RV32`: reads 32-bits from- `hi`and 32-bits from- `lo`to create a 64-bit value
- `RV64`: reads a 64-bit value from- `lo`

---

# read_csr_as in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_csr_as.html

```
macro_rules! read_csr_as {
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $sentinel:tt) => { ... };
    (base $register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $sentinel:tt, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Convenience macro to read a CSR register value as a `register` type.

The `register` type must be a defined type in scope of the macro call.

# read_csr_rv32 in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_csr_rv32.html

```
macro_rules! read_csr_rv32 {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

`RV32`: Convenience macro to wrap the `csrrs` assembly instruction for reading a CSR register.

This macro should generally not be called directly.

Instead, use the [read_csr_as_rv32](https://docs.rs/macro.read_csr_as_rv32.html) or [read_csr_as_usize_rv32](https://docs.rs/macro.read_csr_as_usize_rv32.html) macros.

# read_only_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_only_csr.html

```
macro_rules! read_only_csr {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr,
     sentinel: $sentinel:tt$(,)?,
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Helper macro to create a read-only CSR type.

The type allows to read the CSR value into memory.

---

# read_write_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_write_csr.html

```
macro_rules! read_write_csr {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Helper macro to create a read-write CSR type.

The type allows to read the CSR value into memory, and update the field values in-memory.

The user can then write the entire bitfield value back into the CSR with a single write.

---

}
```
## Expand description

# write_composite_csr in riscv - Rust

}
```
## Expand description

Convenience macro to write a composite value to a CSR register.

- `RV32`: writes 32-bits into- `hi`and 32-bits into- `lo`to create a 64-bit value
- `RV64`: writes a 64-bit value into- `lo`

macro_rules! write_only_csr_field {
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit_start:literal..=$bit_end:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: [$bit_start:literal : $bit_end:literal]$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident,
     $field_ty:ident: [$field_start:literal : $field_end:literal]$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines field accessor functions for a write-only CSR type.

# ExceptionNumber in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32i-unknown-none-elf/riscv/trait.ExceptionNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait ExceptionNumber: `[Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) {
    const [MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER): [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
    // Required methods
    fn [number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.number)(self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
[from_number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.from_number)(value: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [Error](https://docs.rs/result/enum.Error.html)>;
}## Expand description

Trait for enums of target-specific exception numbers.

This trait should be implemented by a peripheral access crate (PAC) on its enum of available
exceptions for a specific device. Alternatively, the `riscv` crate provides a default
implementation for the RISC-V ISA. Each variant must convert to a `usize` of its exception number.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- This trait must only be implemented on the `riscv`crate or on a PAC of a RISC-V target.
- This trait must only be implemented on enums of exceptions.
- Each enum variant must represent a distinct value (no duplicates are permitted),
- Each enum variant must always return the same value (do not change at runtime).
- All the exception numbers must be less than or equal to `MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER`.
- `MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER`must coincide with the highest allowed exception number.

## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/riscv/0.16.1/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/

## Expand description

Low level access to RISC-V processors

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv)Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.60 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

This crate provides:

- Access to core registers like `mstatus`or`mcause`.
- Interrupt manipulation mechanisms.
- Wrappers around assembly instructions like `WFI`.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

[§](https://docs.rs#s-mode)`s-mode`

This feature re-exports in `interrupt` S-mode interrupt functions defined in `interrupt::supervisor`.
By default, the crate assumes that the target is running in M-mode.
Thus, `interrupt` re-exports the M-mode functions defined in `interrupt::machine`.

[§](https://docs.rs#critical-section-single-hart)`critical-section-single-hart`

This feature enables a [ critical-section](https://github.com/rust-embedded/critical-section)
implementation suitable for single-hart targets, based on disabling interrupts globally.
This feature uses S-mode interrupt handling if the

`s-mode` feature is enabled, and M-mode otherwise.It is **unsound** to enable it on multi-hart targets,
and may cause functional problems in systems where some interrupts must NOT be disabled
or critical sections are managed as part of an RTOS. In these cases, you should use
a target-specific implementation instead, typically provided by a HAL or RTOS crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#rt)`rt`

This feature enables code related to [ riscv-rt](https://github.com/rust-embedded/riscv/tree/master/riscv-rt)
runtime support in the

`riscv::pac_enum` macro. Namely, it enables the generation of
trap handler functions and dispatch functions.[§](https://docs.rs#rt-v-trap)`rt-v-trap`

This feature enables code related to vectored trap handling in addition to the `rt` feature.
Namely, it enables the generation of a vector table and the corresponding assembly code for core interrupts.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [asm](https://docs.rs/asm/index.html)
- Assembly instructions
- [bits](https://docs.rs/bits/index.html)
- [delay](https://docs.rs/delay/index.html)
- Delay devices and providers
- [interrupt](https://docs.rs/interrupt/index.html)
- Interrupts
- [register](https://docs.rs/register/index.html)
- RISC-V CSR’s
- [result](https://docs.rs/result/index.html)

# riscv::register - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/register/index.html

## Expand description

RISC-V CSR’s

The following registers are not available on 64-bit implementations.

- cycleh
- timeh
- instreth
- hpmcounter<3-31>h
- mcycleh
- minstreth
- mhpmcounter<3-31>h
- mstatush

[§](https://docs.rs#on-floating-point-csrs)On Floating-Point CSRs

We are deliberately *not* providing instructions that could change the floating-point rounding
mode or exception behavior or read the accrued exceptions flags: `frcsr`, `fscsr`, `fsrm`,
`frflags`, `fsflags`.

Rust makes no guarantees whatsoever about the contents of the accrued exceptions register: Rust floating-point operations may or may not result in this register getting updated with exception state, and the register can change between two invocations of this function even when no floating-point operations appear in the source code (since floating-point operations appearing earlier or later can be reordered).

Modifying the rounding mode leads to **immediate Undefined Behavior**: Rust assumes that the
default rounding mode is always set and will optimize accordingly. This even applies when the
rounding mode is altered and later reset to its original value without any floating-point
operations appearing in the source code between those operations (since floating-point
operations appearing earlier or later can be reordered).

If you need to perform some floating-point operations and check whether they raised an exception, use a single inline assembly block for the entire sequence of operations.

If you need to perform some floating-point operations under a different rounding mode, use a single inline assembly block and make sure to restore the original rounding mode before the end of the block.

# clear in riscv - Rust

# Macro clear

[Source](../src/riscv/register/macros.rs.html#376-404) ```
macro_rules! clear {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

This macro is intended for use with the [clear_csr](macro.clear_csr.html) or [set_clear_csr](macro.set_clear_csr.html) macros.

macro_rules! read_csr_as {
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $sentinel:tt) => { ... };
    (base $register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };

}
```
## Expand description

Convenience macro to read a CSR register value as a `register` type.

The `register` type must be a defined type in scope of the macro call.

# read_only_csr_field in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_only_csr_field.html

```
macro_rules! read_only_csr_field {
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit_start:literal..=$bit_end:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: [$bit_start:literal : $bit_end:literal]$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident,
     $field_ty:ident: [$field_start:literal : $field_end:literal]$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines field accessor functions for a read-only CSR type.

# read_write_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_write_csr.html

```
macro_rules! read_write_csr {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Helper macro to create a read-write CSR type.

The type allows to read the CSR value into memory, and update the field values in-memory.

The user can then write the entire bitfield value back into the CSR with a single write.

---

# read_write_csr_field in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_write_csr_field.html

macro_rules! read_write_csr_field {
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit:literal$(,)?
     ) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit_start:literal ..= $bit_end:literal$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: [$bit_start:literal : $bit_end:literal]$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident,
     $field_ty:ident: [$field_start:literal : $field_end:literal],
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines field accessor functions for a read-write CSR type.

# singleton in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.singleton.html

```
macro_rules! singleton {
    (: $ty:ty = $expr:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro to create a mutable reference to a statically allocated value

This macro returns a value with type `Option<&'static mut $ty>`. `Some($expr)` will be returned
the first time the macro is executed; further calls will return `None`. To avoid `unwrap`ping a
`None` variant the caller must ensure that the macro is called from a function that’s executed
at most once in the whole lifetime of the program.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

This macro requires a `critical-section` implementation to be set. For most single-hart systems,
you can enable the `critical-section-single-hart` feature for this crate. For other systems, you
have to provide one from elsewhere, typically your chip’s HAL crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use riscv::singleton;
fn main() {
    // OK if `main` is executed only once
    let x: &'static mut bool = singleton!(: bool = false).unwrap();
    let y = alias();
    // BAD this second call to `alias` will definitively `panic!`
    let y_alias = alias();
}
fn alias() -> &'static mut bool {
    singleton!(: bool = false).unwrap()
}
```

---

# write_composite_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.write_composite_csr.html

```
macro_rules! write_composite_csr {
    ($hi:expr, $lo:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Convenience macro to write a composite value to a CSR register.

- `RV32`: writes 32-bits into- `hi`and 32-bits into- `lo`to create a 64-bit value
- `RV64`: writes a 64-bit value into- `lo`

---

# write_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.write_csr.html

# Macro write_csr

[Source](../src/riscv/register/macros.rs.html#150-178) ```
macro_rules! write_csr {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Convenience macro to wrap the `csrrw` assembly instruction for writing to CSR registers.

This macro should generally not be called directly.

Instead, use the [write_csr_as_usize](macro.write_csr_as_usize.html) macro.

---

# write_only_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.write_only_csr.html

```
macro_rules! write_only_csr {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Helper macro to create a read-only CSR type.

The type allows to read the CSR value into memory.

```

     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}

# write_only_csr_field in riscv - Rust

macro_rules! write_only_csr_field {
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit_start:literal..=$bit_end:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: [$bit_start:literal : $bit_end:literal]$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident,
     $field_ty:ident: [$field_start:literal : $field_end:literal]$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines field accessor functions for a write-only CSR type.

# CoreInterruptNumber in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/trait.CoreInterruptNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait CoreInterruptNumber: `[InterruptNumber](https://docs.rs/trait.InterruptNumber.html) { }## Expand description

Marker trait for enums of target-specific core interrupt numbers.

Core interrupts are interrupts are retrieved from the `mcause` CSR. Usually, vectored mode is
only available for core interrupts. The `riscv` crate provides a default implementation for
the RISC-V ISA. However, a PAC may override the default implementation if the target has a
different interrupt numbering scheme (e.g., ESP32C3).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

Each enum variant must represent a valid core interrupt number read from the `mcause` CSR.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

## Implementors[§](https://docs.rs#implementors)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/riscv/interrupt/machine.rs.html#44)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-CoreInterruptNumber-for-Interrupt)

### impl [CoreInterruptNumber](https://docs.rs/trait.CoreInterruptNumber.html) for riscv::interrupt::machine::[Interrupt](https://docs.rs/interrupt/machine/enum.Interrupt.html)

SAFETY: `Interrupt` represents the standard RISC-V core interrupts

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/riscv/interrupt/supervisor.rs.html#38)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-CoreInterruptNumber-for-Interrupt-1)

### impl [CoreInterruptNumber](https://docs.rs/trait.CoreInterruptNumber.html) for riscv::interrupt::supervisor::[Interrupt](https://docs.rs/interrupt/supervisor/enum.Interrupt.html)

SAFETY: `Interrupt` represents the standard RISC-V core interrupts

# ExceptionNumber in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/trait.ExceptionNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait ExceptionNumber: `[Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) {
    const [MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER): [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
    // Required methods
    fn [number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.number)(self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
[from_number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.from_number)(value: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [Error](https://docs.rs/result/enum.Error.html)>;
}## Expand description

Trait for enums of target-specific exception numbers.

This trait should be implemented by a peripheral access crate (PAC) on its enum of available
exceptions for a specific device. Alternatively, the `riscv` crate provides a default
implementation for the RISC-V ISA. Each variant must convert to a `usize` of its exception number.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- This trait must only be implemented on the `riscv`crate or on a PAC of a RISC-V target.
- This trait must only be implemented on enums of exceptions.
- Each enum variant must represent a distinct value (no duplicates are permitted),
- Each enum variant must always return the same value (do not change at runtime).
- All the exception numbers must be less than or equal to `MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER`.
- `MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER`must coincide with the highest allowed exception number.

## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# ExternalInterruptNumber in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/trait.ExternalInterruptNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait ExternalInterruptNumber: `[InterruptNumber](https://docs.rs/trait.InterruptNumber.html) { }## Expand description

Marker trait for enums of target-specific external interrupt numbers.

External interrupts are interrupts caused by external sources (e.g., GPIO, UART, SPI).
External interrupts are **not** retrieved from the `mcause` CSR.
Instead, RISC-V processors have a single core interrupt for all external interrupts.
An additional peripheral (e.g., PLIC) is used to multiplex the external interrupts.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

Each enum variant must represent a valid external interrupt number.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# pac_enum in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/riscv/attr.pac_enum.html

`#[pac_enum]`## Expand description

Attribute-like macro that implements the traits of the `riscv-types` crate for a given enum.

As these traits are unsafe, the macro must be called with the `unsafe` keyword followed by the trait name.
In this way, we warn callers that they must comply with the requirements of the trait.

The trait name must be one of `ExceptionNumber`, `CoreInterruptNumber`, `ExternalInterruptNumber`,
`PriorityNumber`, or `HartIdNumber`.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

Crates using this macro must depend on the `riscv` crate, as the generated code references it.

If the `rt` feature is enabled, the generated code may also include the necessary runtime support
for interrupt and exception handling. Thus, the calling crate must also depend on the `riscv-rt` crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

The struct to be implemented must comply with the requirements of the specified trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use riscv::*;
#[repr(usize)]
#[pac_enum(unsafe ExceptionNumber)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum Exception {
    E1 = 1,
    E3 = 3,
}
assert_eq!(Exception::E1.number(), 1);
assert_eq!(Exception::E3.number(), 3);
assert_eq!(Exception::from_number(1), Ok(Exception::E1));
assert_eq!(Exception::from_number(2), Err(2));
assert_eq!(Exception::from_number(3), Ok(Exception::E3));
assert_eq!(Exception::MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER, 3);
```

---

# riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/riscv/0.16.1/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/

## Expand description

Low level access to RISC-V processors

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv)Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.60 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

This crate provides:

- Access to core registers like `mstatus`or`mcause`.
- Interrupt manipulation mechanisms.
- Wrappers around assembly instructions like `WFI`.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

[§](https://docs.rs#s-mode)`s-mode`

This feature re-exports in `interrupt` S-mode interrupt functions defined in `interrupt::supervisor`.
By default, the crate assumes that the target is running in M-mode.
Thus, `interrupt` re-exports the M-mode functions defined in `interrupt::machine`.

[§](https://docs.rs#critical-section-single-hart)`critical-section-single-hart`

This feature enables a [ critical-section](https://github.com/rust-embedded/critical-section)
implementation suitable for single-hart targets, based on disabling interrupts globally.
This feature uses S-mode interrupt handling if the

`s-mode` feature is enabled, and M-mode otherwise.It is **unsound** to enable it on multi-hart targets,
and may cause functional problems in systems where some interrupts must NOT be disabled
or critical sections are managed as part of an RTOS. In these cases, you should use
a target-specific implementation instead, typically provided by a HAL or RTOS crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#rt)`rt`

This feature enables code related to [ riscv-rt](https://github.com/rust-embedded/riscv/tree/master/riscv-rt)
runtime support in the

`riscv::pac_enum` macro. Namely, it enables the generation of
trap handler functions and dispatch functions.[§](https://docs.rs#rt-v-trap)`rt-v-trap`

This feature enables code related to vectored trap handling in addition to the `rt` feature.
Namely, it enables the generation of a vector table and the corresponding assembly code for core interrupts.

# riscv::asm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/asm/index.html

## Expand description

Assembly instructions

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [delay](https://docs.rs/fn.delay.html)
- Blocks the program for *at least*`cycles`CPU cycles.
- [ebreak](https://docs.rs/fn.ebreak.html)- ⚠
- `EBREAK`instruction wrapper
- [ecall](https://docs.rs/fn.ecall.html)- ⚠
- `ECALL`instruction wrapper
- [fence](https://docs.rs/fn.fence.html)
- `FENCE`instruction wrapper
- [fence_i](https://docs.rs/fn.fence_i.html)
- `FENCE.I`instruction wrapper
- [nop](https://docs.rs/fn.nop.html)
- `NOP`instruction wrapper
- [sfence_](https://docs.rs/fn.sfence_vma.html)- vma
- `SFENCE.VMA`instruction wrapper
- [sfence_](https://docs.rs/fn.sfence_vma_all.html)- vma_ - all
- `SFENCE.VMA`instruction wrapper (all address spaces and page table levels)
- [wfi](https://docs.rs/fn.wfi.html)
- `WFI`instruction wrapper

# clear in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.clear.html

# Macro clear

[Source](../src/riscv/register/macros.rs.html#376-404) ```
macro_rules! clear {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Convenience macro around the `csrrc` assembly instruction to clear the CSR register.

This macro is intended for use with the [clear_csr](macro.clear_csr.html) or [set_clear_csr](macro.set_clear_csr.html) macros.

---

# csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.csr.html

```
macro_rules! csr {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])*
     $ty:ident,
     $mask:expr) => { ... };
}
```

---

# read_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_csr.html

# Macro read_csr

[Source](../src/riscv/register/macros.rs.html#7-35) ```
macro_rules! read_csr {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Convenience macro to wrap the `csrrs` assembly instruction for reading a CSR register.

This macro should generally not be called directly.

Instead, use the [read_csr_as](macro.read_csr_as.html) or [read_csr_as_usize](macro.read_csr_as_usize.html) macros.

---

# read_csr_as in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_csr_as.html

```
macro_rules! read_csr_as {
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $sentinel:tt) => { ... };
    (base $register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
    ($register:ident, $csr_number:literal, $sentinel:tt, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Convenience macro to read a CSR register value as a `register` type.

The `register` type must be a defined type in scope of the macro call.

---

`RV32`: Convenience macro to read a CSR register value as a `usize`

---

# read_csr_rv32 in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_csr_rv32.html

```
macro_rules! read_csr_rv32 {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

`RV32`: Convenience macro to wrap the `csrrs` assembly instruction for reading a CSR register.

This macro should generally not be called directly.

Instead, use the [read_csr_as_rv32](https://docs.rs/macro.read_csr_as_rv32.html) or [read_csr_as_usize_rv32](https://docs.rs/macro.read_csr_as_usize_rv32.html) macros.

---

# read_only_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_only_csr.html

```
macro_rules! read_only_csr {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr,
     sentinel: $sentinel:tt$(,)?,
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Helper macro to create a read-only CSR type.

The type allows to read the CSR value into memory.

---

# read_write_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_write_csr.html

```
macro_rules! read_write_csr {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])+
     $ty:ident: $csr:expr,
     mask: $mask:expr$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Helper macro to create a read-write CSR type.

The type allows to read the CSR value into memory, and update the field values in-memory.

The user can then write the entire bitfield value back into the CSR with a single write.

---

# read_write_csr_as_usize in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_write_csr_as_usize.html

```
macro_rules! read_write_csr_as_usize {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    (safe $csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
    (safe $csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```

# singleton in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.singleton.html

```
macro_rules! singleton {
    (: $ty:ty = $expr:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro to create a mutable reference to a statically allocated value

This macro returns a value with type `Option<&'static mut $ty>`. `Some($expr)` will be returned
the first time the macro is executed; further calls will return `None`. To avoid `unwrap`ping a
`None` variant the caller must ensure that the macro is called from a function that’s executed
at most once in the whole lifetime of the program.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

This macro requires a `critical-section` implementation to be set. For most single-hart systems,
you can enable the `critical-section-single-hart` feature for this crate. For other systems, you
have to provide one from elsewhere, typically your chip’s HAL crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use riscv::singleton;
fn main() {
    // OK if `main` is executed only once
    let x: &'static mut bool = singleton!(: bool = false).unwrap();
    let y = alias();
    // BAD this second call to `alias` will definitively `panic!`
    let y_alias = alias();
}
fn alias() -> &'static mut bool {
    singleton!(: bool = false).unwrap()
}
```

---

# write_only_csr_field in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.write_only_csr_field.html

```
macro_rules! write_only_csr_field {
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: $bit_start:literal..=$bit_end:literal$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident: [$bit_start:literal : $bit_end:literal]$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($ty:ident,
     $(#[$field_doc:meta])+
     $field:ident,
     $field_ty:ident: [$field_start:literal : $field_end:literal]$(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines field accessor functions for a write-only CSR type.

# ExceptionNumber in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/trait.ExceptionNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait ExceptionNumber: `[Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) {
    const [MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER): [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
    // Required methods
    fn [number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.number)(self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
[from_number](https://docs.rs#tymethod.from_number)(value: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [Error](https://docs.rs/result/enum.Error.html)>;
}## Expand description

Trait for enums of target-specific exception numbers.

This trait should be implemented by a peripheral access crate (PAC) on its enum of available
exceptions for a specific device. Alternatively, the `riscv` crate provides a default
implementation for the RISC-V ISA. Each variant must convert to a `usize` of its exception number.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- This trait must only be implemented on the `riscv`crate or on a PAC of a RISC-V target.
- This trait must only be implemented on enums of exceptions.
- Each enum variant must represent a distinct value (no duplicates are permitted),
- Each enum variant must always return the same value (do not change at runtime).
- All the exception numbers must be less than or equal to `MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER`.
- `MAX_EXCEPTION_NUMBER`must coincide with the highest allowed exception number.

## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# ExternalInterruptNumber in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/trait.ExternalInterruptNumber.html

`pub unsafe trait ExternalInterruptNumber: `[InterruptNumber](https://docs.rs/trait.InterruptNumber.html) { }## Expand description

Marker trait for enums of target-specific external interrupt numbers.

External interrupts are interrupts caused by external sources (e.g., GPIO, UART, SPI).
External interrupts are **not** retrieved from the `mcause` CSR.
Instead, RISC-V processors have a single core interrupt for all external interrupts.
An additional peripheral (e.g., PLIC) is used to multiplex the external interrupts.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

Each enum variant must represent a valid external interrupt number.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

# riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/riscv/0.16.1/riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/

## Expand description

Low level access to RISC-V processors

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv)Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.60 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

This crate provides:

- Access to core registers like `mstatus`or`mcause`.
- Interrupt manipulation mechanisms.
- Wrappers around assembly instructions like `WFI`.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

[§](https://docs.rs#s-mode)`s-mode`

This feature re-exports in `interrupt` S-mode interrupt functions defined in `interrupt::supervisor`.
By default, the crate assumes that the target is running in M-mode.
Thus, `interrupt` re-exports the M-mode functions defined in `interrupt::machine`.

[§](https://docs.rs#critical-section-single-hart)`critical-section-single-hart`

This feature enables a [ critical-section](https://github.com/rust-embedded/critical-section)
implementation suitable for single-hart targets, based on disabling interrupts globally.
This feature uses S-mode interrupt handling if the

`s-mode` feature is enabled, and M-mode otherwise.It is **unsound** to enable it on multi-hart targets,
and may cause functional problems in systems where some interrupts must NOT be disabled
or critical sections are managed as part of an RTOS. In these cases, you should use
a target-specific implementation instead, typically provided by a HAL or RTOS crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#rt)`rt`

This feature enables code related to [ riscv-rt](https://github.com/rust-embedded/riscv/tree/master/riscv-rt)
runtime support in the

`riscv::pac_enum` macro. Namely, it enables the generation of
trap handler functions and dispatch functions.[§](https://docs.rs#rt-v-trap)`rt-v-trap`

This feature enables code related to vectored trap handling in addition to the `rt` feature.
Namely, it enables the generation of a vector table and the corresponding assembly code for core interrupts.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [asm](https://docs.rs/asm/index.html)
- Assembly instructions
- [bits](https://docs.rs/bits/index.html)
- [delay](https://docs.rs/delay/index.html)
- Delay devices and providers
- [interrupt](https://docs.rs/interrupt/index.html)
- Interrupts
- [register](https://docs.rs/register/index.html)
- RISC-V CSR’s
- [result](https://docs.rs/result/index.html)

### Structs

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf/src/riscv/lib.rs.html

# riscv/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Low level access to RISC-V processors
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! # Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.60 and up. It *might*
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! # Features
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! This crate provides:
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! - Access to core registers like `mstatus` or `mcause`.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! - Interrupt manipulation mechanisms.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! - Wrappers around assembly instructions like `WFI`.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! # Optional features
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! ## `s-mode`
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! This feature re-exports in `interrupt` S-mode interrupt functions defined in `interrupt::supervisor`.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! By default, the crate assumes that the target is running in M-mode.
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! Thus, `interrupt` re-exports the M-mode functions defined in `interrupt::machine`.
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! ## `critical-section-single-hart`
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! This feature enables a [`critical-section`](https://github.com/rust-embedded/critical-section)
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! implementation suitable for single-hart targets, based on disabling interrupts globally.
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! This feature uses S-mode interrupt handling if the `s-mode` feature is enabled, and M-mode otherwise.
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! It is **unsound** to enable it on multi-hart targets,
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! and may cause functional problems in systems where some interrupts must NOT be disabled
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! or critical sections are managed as part of an RTOS. In these cases, you should use
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! a target-specific implementation instead, typically provided by a HAL or RTOS crate.
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! ## `rt`
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! This feature enables code related to [`riscv-rt`](https://github.com/rust-embedded/riscv/tree/master/riscv-rt)
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! runtime support in the `riscv::pac_enum` macro. Namely, it enables the generation of
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! trap handler functions and dispatch functions.
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! ## `rt-v-trap`
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! This feature enables code related to vectored trap handling in addition to the `rt` feature.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! Namely, it enables the generation of a vector table and the corresponding assembly code for core interrupts.
[45](https://docs.rs#45)
[46](https://docs.rs#46)#![no_std]
[47](https://docs.rs#47)#![allow(clippy::missing_safety_doc)]
[48](https://docs.rs#48)#![allow(clippy::eq_op)]
[49](https://docs.rs#49)#![allow(clippy::identity_op)]
[50](https://docs.rs#50)
[51](https://docs.rs#51)pub use pastey::paste;
[52](https://docs.rs#52)
[53](https://docs.rs#53)pub mod asm;
[54](https://docs.rs#54)pub mod bits;
[55](https://docs.rs#55)pub mod delay;
[56](https://docs.rs#56)pub mod interrupt;
[57](https://docs.rs#57)pub mod register;
[58](https://docs.rs#58)
[59](https://docs.rs#59)// Re-export crates of the RISC-V ecosystem
[60](https://docs.rs#60)#[cfg(feature = "riscv-macros")]
[61](https://docs.rs#61)pub use riscv_macros::pac_enum;
[62](https://docs.rs#62)pub use riscv_types::*;
[63](https://docs.rs#63)
[64](https://docs.rs#64)#[macro_use]
[65](https://docs.rs#65)mod macros;
[66](https://docs.rs#66)
[67](https://docs.rs#67)#[cfg(all(
[68](https://docs.rs#68)    any(target_arch = "riscv32", target_arch = "riscv64"),
[69](https://docs.rs#69)    feature = "critical-section-single-hart"
[70](https://docs.rs#70)))]
[71](https://docs.rs#71)mod critical_section;
[72](https://docs.rs#72)
[73](https://docs.rs#73)/// Used to reexport items for use in macros. Do not use directly.
[74](https://docs.rs#74)/// Not covered by semver guarantees.
[75](https://docs.rs#75)#[doc(hidden)]
[76](https://docs.rs#76)pub mod _export {
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    pub use critical_section;
[78](https://docs.rs#78)}

# read_composite_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_composite_csr.html

```
macro_rules! read_composite_csr {
    ($hi:expr, $lo:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Convenience macro to read a composite value from a CSR register.

- `RV32`: reads 32-bits from- `hi`and 32-bits from- `lo`to create a 64-bit value
- `RV64`: reads a 64-bit value from- `lo`

---

# read_csr in riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/riscv/latest/target-redirect/riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf/riscv/macro.read_csr.html

# Macro read_csr

[Source](../src/riscv/register/macros.rs.html#7-35) ```
macro_rules! read_csr {
    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };
    ($csr_number:literal, $($cfg:meta),*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Convenience macro to wrap the `csrrs` assembly instruction for reading a CSR register.

This macro should generally not be called directly.

Instead, use the [read_csr_as](macro.read_csr_as.html) or [read_csr_as_usize](macro.read_csr_as_usize.html) macros.

---

    ($csr_number:literal) => { ... };

}
```

# read_csr_rv32 in riscv - Rust

macro_rules! read_csr_rv32 {

## Expand description

`RV32`: Convenience macro to wrap the `csrrs` assembly instruction for reading a CSR register.

This macro should generally not be called directly.

Instead, use the [read_csr_as_rv32](https://docs.rs/macro.read_csr_as_rv32.html) or [read_csr_as_usize_rv32](https://docs.rs/macro.read_csr_as_usize_rv32.html) macros.
